predecessors.name: Vakataka dynasty
predecessors.text: Vidarbha, passed "from the Vakatakas and Vishnukundinas"

ledger.x: c. 550: Krishnaraja founds the Kalachuri power at Mahishmati. "Krishnaraja (r. c. 550-575) is the earliest known Kalachuri ruler"; around 550 "Malwa lacked a strong ruler, Vakataka rule in Maharashtra had ended, and Maitraka power in Gujarat was declining." The infobox gives no dates; its ruler list runs from 550 to…
c. 550: the Kalachuris take northern Konkan. "Konkan was taken by the mid-6th century, succeeding the Traikutakas" (page); the Traikutaka dossier ends c. 550.
c. 550: Vidarbha passes to the Kalachuris. "Vidarbha passed to them from the Vakatakas and Vishnukundinas"; the page gives no date, and the Vakataka dossier ends c. 510 (sa-02-d).

c. 597: Shankaragana takes Ujjain. "took Ujjain around 597 from Mahasenagupta"; a 597 CE inscription issued from Ujjain records a grant near Abhona. A footnote dates "the Maitraka loss of Ujjain to 616-617", which the page does not reconcile.

c. 608: Buddharaja takes Vidisha. "he took Vidisha around 608"; a footnote dates the occupation of Vidisha to 608-609; grants of 609-611 are issued from his camps at Vidisha and Anandapura. The page does not say who held Vidisha.

c. 625: the Kalachuri rule ends under Chalukya pressure. "Buddharaja's reign ended sometime before 630 CE, when Chalukya inscriptions show control of the Nashik area"; the infobox ruler list ends 625; Mangalesha attacked from the south in Buddharaja's reign and Pulakeshin II (possibly his nephew) is also linked to the…

wars.name: Chalukya conquest of the Kalachuris
wars.outcome: Mangalesha and Pulakeshin II defeat Buddharaja; the Nashik area is Chalukya before 630 and the Kalachuris are Chalukya feudatories in 687.

certainty.note: No border is given; the Kalachuri lands are named by region and by the cities taken (Ujjain, Vidisha).
